https://hungarytoday.hu/sziget-festival-.text: While Ordinary Hungarians are Told to Save Energy, the Sziget Festival Gets a Green Light With the Paks Nuclear Power Plant facing a potential shutdown, Hungary is concerned about the stability of its national power grid . However, the organizers of the Sziget Festival in Budapest have given the all-clear. Thanks to years of upgrades and its own emergency generators, the major event, taking place from August 11 to 15, will operate completely independently of the public grid. In recent days, the situation of the Hungarian energy system has dominated the headlines. The reason for this is the announcement of extraordinary measures in connection with the expected complete shutdown of the Paks Nuclear Power Plant. While fears of power shortages were voiced among the public, the organizers of the Sziget Festival stepped in to reassure the public. The festival does not place a strain on the Hungarian power grid and does not jeopardize the national power supply in any way,” according to their statement. The organizers have built up a robust infrastructure in recent years. The festival has a state-of-the-art, generator-backed power supply system. In the event of a nationwide power outage or grid constraints, the festival grounds on Hajógyári Island in Budapest can be completely disconnected from the central grid if necessary. In the event of an emergency, the energy required for operations is generated entirely by our own system. Both the safety of our visitors and the uninterrupted execution of the entire program are guaranteed at all times,” the statement reads. Sziget Festival. Photo: Hungary Today In addition to ensuring reliability, the organizers of the Sziget Festival are committed to conserving resources. Thanks to technological innovations in recent years, total energy consumption has been steadily reduced. The widespread use of modern LED lighting and highly efficient sound systems on the stages has played a key role in this. The festival is also taking a sustainable approach to water management. Throughout the festival grounds, free drinking water refill stations encourage visitors to use reusable bottles, thereby reducing plastic waste. Even the water used to control dust on the paths is not wasted. It seeps through the natural gravel bed of Hajógyári Island directly back into the Danube. The announcement confirms earlier reports that the festival remains fully operational even under extreme grid conditions. From August 11 to 15, hundreds of thousands of music and culture enthusiasts from around the world can look forward to a smooth festival experience on the Danube Island. For Hungary as a whole, however, the outlook remains uncertain , with the ongoing heatwave expected to keep electricity demand elevated and the broader energy situation under pressure for the foreseeable future.
